cards.front: In non-shockable rhythms (PEA/asystole), adrenaline 1 mg IV is given immediately and then every [___] minutes.
cards.context:
In non-shockable arrest, adrenaline goes *immediately* because there's no defibrillation to prioritise — α-1 vasoconstriction raises diastolic aortic pressure, which is what perfuses the coronaries during CPR.

Contrast with shockable rhythms: there, defibrillation comes first, adrenaline is *delayed* until after the 2nd shock so the early shocks aren't competing with the catecholamine surge. Same dose either way (1 mg IV/IO).

cards.front: Severely elevated lactate threshold: above [___] (triggers aggressive resuscitation in sepsis).
cards.context:
Surviving Sepsis defines a hard lactate threshold above which mortality rises sharply and the Hour-1 bundle (cultures, broad-spectrum antibiotics, 30 mL/kg crystalloid.

That threshold is set high enough to identify severe tissue hypoperfusion — at this level, cellular oxygen debt is established even if BP looks reassuring.

cards.front: After a significant overdose of an analgesic that targets COX but has a narrow hepatic-safety margin, management includes: check paracetamol levels at 4 hours, start NAC if indicated by the nomogram, and arrange [___] review before discharge.
cards.context:
Paracetamol overdose looks deceptively boring in the first 24 h — nausea, vague abdominal discomfort, normal observations and LFTs. Hepatic injury declares itself at 24-72 h, often after the patient has been discharged.

Protocol: plot serum paracetamol drawn at 4+ h post-ingestion (earlier values can't be interpreted) on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram; above the line.

cards.front: Dobutamine infusion range: 2.5-20 mcg/kg/min; monitor for [___].
cards.context:
Dobutamine's β₁ inotropy is dose-dependent and so are its β₁-mediated arrhythmias — AF and VT become much more likely above ~10 mcg/kg/min.

The β₂ vasodilation can drop MAP by 5-10 mmHg in the first hour, so dobutamine is usually paired with noradrenaline in cardiogenic shock unless the patient is hypertensive at baseline.

cards.front: Endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion stroke can be performed up to [___] hours from onset, based on the DAWN and DEFUSE-3 trials.
cards.context:
Endovascular thrombectomy is standard of care for large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke involving proximal anterior circulation (ICA, M1 MCA).

NNT ~2.6 for functional independence. CT angiography identifies clot location.

cards.front: First-line treatment for status epilepticus without IV access is midazolam [___] mg IM.
cards.context:
The RAMPART trial (NEJM 2012) showed IM midazolam (10 mg) terminates pre-hospital status as effectively as IV lorazepam (4 mg), with faster delivery (no IV needed).

It is a major win in the prehospital setting, where IV access wastes critical minutes.

Each minute of ongoing seizure causes neuronal injury and reduces benzodiazepine receptor responsiveness (internalisation), so dose adequately and dose early. Under-dosing is the most common error.

cards.front: First-line therapy for haemorrhagic shock: blood products and [___].
cards.context:
The lethal triad — coagulopathy, acidosis, hypothermia — is worsened by crystalloid: dilutes clotting factors, drops temperature, worsens acidosis.

Blood is a stop-gap. Without source control (surgical, IR, endoscopic) even unlimited transfusion can't keep up.

cards.front: NAC anaphylactoid reactions are infusion-rate-dependent (not true allergy). Management: stop NAC, give antihistamine, then recommence at a [___] infusion.
cards.context:
NAC commonly causes flushing, urticaria, wheeze, or hypotension during the loading dose — but this is an anaphylactoid reaction (direct mast cell degranulation), not true IgE-mediated anaphylaxis.

Management: stop infusion, antihistamine (+ bronchodilator if wheezing), wait for settling, restart same NAC at slower rate. Don't switch agents or label 'allergic to NAC' — no equivalent paracetamol antidote.

cards.front: Delirium in sepsis is driven by systemic inflammation causing breakdown of the [___].
cards.context: This neuroinflammatory cascade causes delirium and explains why confusion often precedes fever in sepsis.

cards.front: Na channel blockade: treat with sodium bicarbonate to target pH [___].
cards.context:
Wide QRS indicates severe sodium channel blockade with arrhythmia risk. Alkalinisation with bicarb increases protein binding and reduces free drug, reversing cardiac toxicity.

Don't wait for arrhythmia to start treatment.

cards.front: Climbing 2 flights of stairs approximates [___], the threshold for adequate surgical fitness.
cards.context:
MET = metabolic equivalent of resting oxygen consumption (~3.5 mL/kg/min). 4 METs corresponds to climbing 2 flights of stairs, walking up a hill.

Below 4 METs (can only walk on flat ground, breathless dressing) suggests poor reserve and warrants formal cardiac assessment before major surgery (CPET, stress testing).

cards.front: In LAST, Intralipid 20% is given as a 1.5 mL/kg bolus then [___] mL/kg/hr infusion.
cards.context:
Intralipid 20% (lipid emulsion) is the LAST antidote: 1.5 mL/kg bolus, then 0.25 mL/kg/min (~15 mL/kg/hr) infusion until haemodynamic recovery. Repeat boluses up to 3 times for ongoing arrest.

The mechanism is 'lipid sink' — the lipophilic local anaesthetic redistributes from cardiac sodium channels into the IV lipid emulsion, restoring conduction.

cards.front: Lignocaine max dose: plain 3 mg/kg; with adrenaline [___].
cards.context: Adrenaline causes local vasoconstriction, slowing systemic absorption and allowing higher total dose. Remember: 1% lignocaine = 10 mg/mL, so 20 mL of 1% = 200 mg.

cards.front: In acute ICH, target SBP is < 140 mmHg (INTERACT-2), while ischaemic stroke uses [___] hypertension.
cards.context:
ICH treatment is HEAD-CONTAINMENT: lower SBP rapidly to <140 to limit haematoma expansion (INTERACT-2 NEJM 2013). Higher pressures continue to drive bleeding through fragile vessel walls.

Ischaemic stroke is the OPPOSITE: permissive hypertension to maintain perfusion of penumbra (the rescuable tissue around the infarct core). Only intervene if BP exceeds 220/120 or 185/110 if planning thrombolysis.

cards.front: Maximum lignocaine dose: 3 mg/kg plain, [___] mg/kg with adrenaline.
cards.context:
Plain lignocaine: 3 mg/kg max. Adrenaline (1:200,000) lifts this to 7 mg/kg by causing local vasoconstriction that slows systemic absorption.

For a 70 kg adult: 210 mg plain, 490 mg with adrenaline. Useful conversion: 1% lignocaine = 10 mg/mL, so 21 mL plain or 49 mL with adrenaline.

cards.front: Suxamethonium is contraindicated in denervation injuries after 24 hours due to risk of fatal [___] from upregulated ACh receptors.
cards.context:
Sux causes a small K⁺ rise in everyone (~0.5 mmol/L) from depolarisation.

Sux then triggers massive K⁺ efflux from a much larger receptor pool, producing rises of 5-10 mmol/L within minutes and lethal hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest.

cards.front: Normal ABG: pH 7.35–7.45, pCO₂ 35–45 mmHg, HCO₃ [___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
Anchor on 7.4 / 40 / 24. VBG offsets: pH ~0.03 lower, pCO₂ ~6 higher, HCO₃ same.

VBG cannot assess PaO₂.

cards.front: Ideal ETT position on CXR: 3-5 cm above the carina ([___] level). Most common malposition is right mainstem intubation.
cards.context:
Right mainstem intubation is the most common ETT malposition because the right main bronchus diverges at a smaller angle from the trachea (25° vs 45° for the left).

Head flexion advances the ETT ~2 cm; extension withdraws it ~2 cm.

cards.front: For post-operative nausea on opioid PCA, first-line antiemetics include [___] (5-HT₃), metoclopramide (D₂), or cyclizine (H₁).
cards.context: When one class fails, add a different class rather than repeating the same one.

cards.front: CPP = MAP − ICP. Target CPP is 60-70 mmHg. ICP threshold for starting tiered therapy is [___] mmHg.
cards.context:
CPP is the driving pressure for cerebral blood flow. The formula is simple but the targets are critical — CPP below 50 causes ischaemia, above 70 increases ARDS risk from vasopressor use.

ICP above 22 mmHg sustained triggers escalation to tiered therapy.

cards.front: In the Chain of Survival, the definitive treatment link for VF/pVT is early [___].
cards.context:
VF/pVT is electrically chaotic — the myocardium is depolarising at random across the whole tissue, so no organised contraction is possible until the entire ventricle is reset.

The shock is the only intervention that terminates VF/pVT — CPR maintains perfusion and drugs improve the chance of successful defibrillation.

cards.front: Adult CPR compression depth should be at least [___] cm at a rate of 100-120 per minute.
cards.context:
ANZCOR adult CPR: compress to at least 5 cm depth (but not >6 cm — going too deep risks rib fracture, sternal injury, and lung contusion) at 100-120/min.

The 100-120/min rate is the trade-off between adequate cerebral and coronary perfusion (lower rates inadequate) and rescuer fatigue / inadequate diastolic filling (higher rates worse).

cards.front: The PAXA pathway uses a 0h and [___]-hour troponin protocol; safe discharge requires both values below the 99th percentile with delta less than 4 ng/L.
cards.context: PAXA uses a 0/3-hour protocol (not 0/2h like PACSA). The delta threshold of <4 ng/L is deliberately conservative — even small troponin changes in a low-risk patient warrant further investigation.

cards.front: Hypertonic saline bolus for severe EAH can be repeated up to [___].
cards.context: Hypertonic saline for severe EAH can be repeated if the first bolus does not improve symptoms, up to a maximum of 3 total doses.

cards.front: Normal HCO₃ range is [___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
HCO₃⁻ 22-26 mmol/L = the metabolic component of acid-base balance. Generated by renal tubular reabsorption (proximal) and regeneration (distal).

Rises in metabolic alkalosis (vomiting strips HCl, diuretics drive H⁺ into urine, mineralocorticoid excess).

cards.front: Emphysema reduces gas transfer by decreasing alveolar [___].
cards.context:
Gas transfer (DLCO) follows Fick's law: rate is proportional to area and partial-pressure gradient, divided by membrane thickness.

Emphysema destroys alveolar walls, merging small alveoli into large bullae — this dramatically reduces the total area available for gas exchange, even though each remaining patch may function normally.

cards.front: Key damage control resuscitation targets: pH greater than 7.2, lactate less than 4 mmol/L, ionised calcium greater than 1.1 mmol/L, and temperature greater than [___]°C.
cards.context:
Resuscitation targets during damage control provide specific endpoints to guide product replacement. These numbers should be checked every 30-60 minutes during active MTP.

TBI patients have higher targets because the injured brain tolerates coagulopathy and anaemia poorly.

cards.front: Levetiracetam dose in status epilepticus is [___] mg/kg IV (max 4.5 g).
cards.context:
Levetiracetam is preferred second-line in status (after benzodiazepines) because it has rapid IV onset, minimal haemodynamic effects, no major drug interactions, and doesn't sedate.

If seizures continue, add a different second-line agent before escalating to anaesthetic induction (refractory status).

cards.front: First-line pharmacological option for delirium agitation (after non-pharmacological measures fail) is low-dose quetiapine; avoid [___] as they worsen delirium.
cards.context:
Pharmacological move in delirium is for safety, not cure — keeps the patient in bed long enough to treat the underlying precipitant.

Benzodiazepines are the wrong tool in almost every case — prolong delirium, deepen sedation, ↑falls + aspiration. Exception: alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal delirium (treats cause).

cards.front: Parkland formula: [___] × weight (kg) × %TBSA = total fluid in first 24 hours.
cards.context: Parkland estimates fluid requirements based on burn surface area — larger burns cause more capillary leak and third-spacing.

cards.front: Massive transfusion is defined as replacement of total blood volume in [___] hours.
cards.context: Massive transfusion is defined as half the blood volume in 4 hours OR total blood volume in 24 hours. The MTP pack typically contains 4 units RBC, 2 units FFP, and considers platelets and tranexamic acid.
